Senses.Explanation: The staff is the walking stick carried by a patched-robed monastic and repeatedly handled as a teaching-seat implement in Chan records. The graphs identify a staff or cane (杖) used for propping or leaning (拄), with a noun-forming suffix (子), and the Blue Cliff Record directly calls it an ordinary implement of a patched-robed monastic (拄杖子是衲僧尋常用底). Bajiao Huiqing's public case gives a staff to one who has one and takes it from one who has none (爾有拄杖子，我與爾拄杖子；爾無拄杖子，我奪爾拄杖子). Yunmen Wenyan hands it over, and the recipient snaps it in two. The physical object is also made a participant in public address: Wuyi Yuanlai says it can distinguish the matter, Ruiyan Zhicai says it teaches the gate of equality day and night, and Ciming Chuyuan makes the buddhas, patriarchs, and old masters become Nanyuan's staff. Yunmen's dragon saying has the staff swallow heaven and earth, then returns explicitly to “just one staff” (只是一條拄杖子). Langya Huijue makes the staff and Mount Sumeru swallow each other, while Cuiyan Kezhen says that picking it up, holding it, and moving it shakes the great-thousand world. Naming is itself repeatedly tested. Yuanwu Keqin records Yunmen Wenyan saying, “when you see a staff, simply call it a staff” (見拄杖子但喚作拄杖子). Fangrong Xi sets positive and negative naming side by side: it must not be called a staff and must not fail to be called one; calling it a staff follows another's interpretation, while not calling it a staff seeks elsewhere (不得喚作拄杖子，不得不喚作拄杖子。喚作拄杖子，則依他作解；不喚作拄杖子，則向外別求). Fenyang Shanzhao says recognizing the staff completes the matter of travelling on foot; Letan Huaicheng, named Sanjiao in the compact witness, says it sends one to hell like an arrow. These opposed formulas do not supply a second definition. The 27,727-hit base form “staff” (拄杖) and the suffixed form “the staff” (拄杖子; 4,111 hits) name the same object across these deployments.
Senses.Note: This is a corpus-wide teaching prop, not an idiom restricted to one individual. The dragon saying is Yunmen Wenyan's, and the give-and-take case is Bajiao Huiqing's; raised-case transmission does not erase their names. Family retest: the base form “staff” (拄杖) names the same object; “staff-head” (拄杖頭) names a related location or point; and the separate entry for the stick or stroke (棒) must preserve its object-versus-blow split. No evidence here warrants splitting the staff's transformations, speech, naming tests, or local equations into different referents.

Occurrences.Kwic: 芭蕉和尚示眾云。爾有拄杖子。我與爾拄杖子。爾無拄杖子。我奪爾拄杖子。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The Gateless Checkpoint (無門關), case 44, “Bajiao's Staff” (芭蕉拄杖), explicitly records Bajiao Huiqing addressing the assembly and giving and taking away the staff.

Occurrences.Kwic: 拄杖子化為龍。吞却乾坤了也。山河大地甚處得來。只是一條拄杖子
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The Blue Cliff Record (佛果圜悟禪師碧巖錄), in Yuanwu Keqin's commentary, quotes Yunmen Wenyan's dragon saying and its explicit return to “just one staff” (只是一條拄杖子) in one contiguous span.

Occurrences.Kwic: 良久，卓拄杖子，云：「拄杖子卻辯得。」
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The Essential Recorded Sayings of Boshan Wuyi (博山無異大師語錄集要) records Wuyi Yuanlai pausing, planting the staff (卓拄杖子), and saying that the staff can distinguish the matter.

Occurrences.Kwic: 見拄杖子但喚作拄杖子。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The Recorded Sayings of Yuanwu Foguo (圓悟佛果禪師語錄), in a small-gathering address by Yuanwu Keqin, explicitly introduces this as a saying by Yunmen Wenyan: “when you see a staff, simply call it a staff” (見拄杖子但喚作拄杖子). Yunmen is the exact quoted speaker; Yuanwu is the later quoter and record owner.

Occurrences.Kwic: 不得喚作拄杖子，不得不喚作拄杖子。喚作拄杖子，則依他作解；不喚作拄杖子，則向外別求。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The Recorded Sayings of Master Fangrong Xi (方融璽禪師語錄), in Fangrong Xi's “Instructions for Travelling on Foot” (行腳垂示), sets calling and not calling the object a staff side by side. Fangrong Xi is not yet on the roster.

Occurrences.Kwic: 拈起拄杖云接取拄杖子僧接得拗作兩截師云直饒與麼也好與三十棒
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Old Recorded Sayings of Venerable Masters (古尊宿語錄), in the record of Yunmen Wenyan, records Yunmen handing over the staff; the recipient breaks it in two, after which Yunmen prescribes thirty blows.

Occurrences.Kwic: 汾陽示眾曰識得拄杖子行脚事畢
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The Linked Collection of Chan Lineage Verse Comments on Old Cases (禪宗頌古聯珠通集) explicitly introduces Fenyang Shanzhao's assembly saying: recognizing the staff completes travelling on foot. This occurrence is trimmed to Fenyang's exact speaker-owned turn.

Occurrences.Kwic: 三角云識得拄杖子入地獄如箭
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The Linked Collection of Chan Lineage Verse Comments on Old Cases (禪宗頌古聯珠通集) attributes the opposed saying to Sanjiao. The parallel in Old Recorded Sayings of Venerable Masters names the speaker Letan Huaicheng and gives the fuller form: recognizing the staff sends one to hell like an arrow. This occurrence is trimmed to Letan's exact speaker-owned turn.

Occurrences.Kwic: 欲知常住性。當觀拄杖子。拄杖子吞却須彌。須彌吞却拄杖子。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The Compendium of the Five Lamps (五燈會元), section on Langya Huijue, records Langya directing the assembly to contemplate the staff, then making the staff and Mount Sumeru swallow each other.

Occurrences.Kwic: 這箇是拄杖子。拈得．把得．動得。三千大千世界。一時搖動。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The Compendium of the Five Lamps (五燈會元), section on Cuiyan Kezhen, records Cuiyan identifying the displayed object as a staff and saying that picking it up, holding it, and moving it shakes the great-thousand world.

Occurrences.Kwic: 這拄杖子晝夜為諸人說平等法門。還聞麼。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The Compendium of the Five Lamps (五燈會元), section on Ruiyan Zhicai, records Ruiyan saying that the staff teaches the gate of equality day and night, then asking whether the assembly hears it. Ruiyan Zhicai is not yet on the roster.

Occurrences.Kwic: 過去諸佛現在諸佛未來諸佛西天二十八祖唐土六祖天下老和尚緫變成南源拄杖子去也
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Old Recorded Sayings of Venerable Masters (古尊宿語錄), in the record of Ciming Chuyuan, records Ciming making the buddhas of the three times, the Indian and Chinese patriarchs, and all old masters become Nanyuan's staff.

Occurrences.Kwic: 拄杖子是衲僧尋常用底。因什麼却道途路不得力。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The Blue Cliff Record (佛果圜悟禪師碧巖錄) records Yuanwu Keqin directly calling the staff an ordinary implement of a patched-robed monk and asking why it is ineffective on the road.

Occurrences.Kwic: 這箇拄杖子是三昧你若識得拄杖子即識得天下老宿
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Old Recorded Sayings of Venerable Masters (古尊宿語錄), in the record of Yunmen Wenyan, records Yunmen locally calling this staff “complete command” (三昧) and tying recognition of it to recognition of the old masters under heaven.

Occurrences.Kwic: 如今在山僧拄杖頭上。指山山崩。指海海竭。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The Recorded Sayings of Yuanwu Foguo (圓悟佛果禪師語錄) records Yuanwu Keqin placing the display at the “staff-head” (拄杖頭). This anchors the related location form without counting it toward standalone headword depth.
